# Bezel Stdlib Gap Review — Consolidated Ranking (2026-07-02)

Synthesized from 9 per-domain surveys (io-fs, text, time, collections, async-concurrency, process-os, numerics-random, serialization-data, diagnostics) against stdlib v0.165.

## Dedup notes

- **PeriodicTimer** appeared in *time* and *async-concurrency* (identical .NET-6 shape recommended in both) → merged, counts as 2×P1.
- **Format-string semantics** appeared in *text* (numeric/date invariant-culture vocabulary) and *numerics-random* (double round-trip guarantee) → merged with **IFormattable** into one formatting cluster (#812, #1339).
- **Base64** (P0) and **Hex** (P1) merged into one binary-text encodings item; **ISerializer.WriteBytes** kept separate but depends on it.
- **Debug.Fail/Unreachable** merged into the **Verify** assertions item; **stack-trace capture** folded alongside (all small Debug/Verify additions).
- **Instant**, **Stopwatch.ElapsedTicks/Frequency**, and **TimeSpan.FromNanoseconds** merged into one monotonic-time cluster (one shared decision: specify tick resolution as nanoseconds).
- Streams are referenced as a dependency by *process-os* (Process stdio), *serialization* (JSON from stream), and the Http proposal (#1376) — the stream family ranks first on dependency order.

## Top briefs

### 1. Concrete stream family (StreamReader/StreamWriter, MemoryStream, CopyToAsync)
The stdlib declares TextReader/TextWriter abstract with no concrete subclass, and has no in-memory Stream — so nothing stream-shaped can be tested without the filesystem, no large file can be read line-by-line, and every downstream consumer (Process stdio, Http #1376 body streaming, future compression) is blocked. Recommended: constructors take `owned stream` so the reader/writer is the sole owner and disposal chains deterministically; a borrow-based construction needs a spec ruling (classes are not borrow-bearing per §9.7) — ship the owned-ctor subset first and file the borrow question. Relates to #645, #1394, proposal 0001 (#1376).

```
public class StreamReader: TextReader { constructor(owned stream: Stream, encoding: Encoding := Encoding.UTF8); }
public class MemoryStream: Stream {
    public static method FromBytes(owned buf: OwningBuffer<byte>): owned MemoryStream;
    public method TakeBytes(): owned OwningBuffer<byte>;   // drains; stream resets
}
// on Stream:
public async method CopyToAsync(destination: Stream, bufferSize: int := 81920, token: CancellationToken := CancellationToken.None): Task;
```

### 2. IFormattable + specified invariant format semantics
Spec §18.5 dispatches `{x:F2}` to "the value's formatter," but no interface exists for user types, and the specifier vocabulary and cultural rules for the intrinsic `ToString(format)` methods are unspecified — including whether `double.ToString()` round-trips. One coordinated fix: an auto-imported single-method interface, retrofitted onto the primitives; a spec amendment enumerating the invariant-culture vocabulary (D/F/E/G/X/P/R numeric; yyyy/MM/dd/HH/mm/ss/fff date), shortest-round-trip as the no-arg double/float default, FormatException on unrecognized specs, and a compile error when a format spec targets a non-IFormattable operand. Relates to #812 (primary) and #1339.

```
public interface IFormattable { method ToString(format: string): string; }   // auto-imported
```

### 3. Base64 + hex encodings
Blocks web auth headers, JWTs, binary-in-JSON, data: URIs, and hash-digest display; totally absent today. Static classes in System.Text (auto-imported), pure functions, FormatException on bad decode input per the defined-fault model; lowercase hex default; Base64Url as a separate static class. This is the prerequisite for #17 (WriteBytes).

```
public static class Base64 {
    public static method Encode(bytes: ReadOnlySpan<byte>): string;
    public static method Decode(s: string): owned Array<byte>;               // FormatException
    public static method TryDecode(s: string, out result: owned Array<byte>): bool;
}
// on Convert: ToHexString(bytes: ReadOnlySpan<byte>): string; FromHexString(s: string): owned Array<byte>;
```

### 4. Serialization eligibility for Guid/DateTime/TimeSpan/DateOnly/TimeOnly
These stdlib records declare neither ISerializable nor IDeserializable, so any record containing a timestamp or ID fails §9.8 synthesis eligibility — which is essentially every real domain model. Fix: hand-written conformances in the stdlib with pinned wire forms (Guid "D" hyphenated; DateTime ISO 8601 matching no-arg ToString(); TimeSpan as ISO 8601 duration; DateOnly `yyyy-MM-dd`; TimeOnly `HH:mm:ss`). Recommend WriteString uniformly for v1 (binary compactness deferred — the binary format is already version-local). Feeds directly into the #703/#550 type-driven serialization plan.

### 5. Child process spawning (System.Diagnostics.Process)
Deferred "open shape" in stdlib §11; blocks build tools, test runners, and anything that shells out. An owned class wrapping the OS handle (destructor kills if never waited); stdio exposed as owned Stream/TextReader fields with borrow accessors and `TakeStdout(): owned TextReader` for handoff; async-only wait (see declined list for the sync form); explicit environment dictionary rather than silent inheritance. Depends on #1 for the stream wrappers.

```
public class Process {
    public static method Start(fileName: string, args: Array<string>, options: ProcessOptions := ...): owned Process;
    public async method WaitForExitAsync(token: CancellationToken := CancellationToken.None): Task<int>;
    public method TakeStdout(): owned TextReader;   // redirected-only
}
```

### 6. Bounded channel with async Send (RFC #809)
An unbounded producer against a slow consumer exhausts the heap — in a no-GC language this is a correctness bug, not a tuning knob. Add a capacity constructor and `SendAsync`; recommend the simpler cancellation ruling: if the token fires while awaiting capacity, the in-flight owned item is disposed and OperationCanceledException raised (defined-fault), rather than inventing a returned-item Task shape. Sendability of Channel<T>/ChannelSender<T> is unchanged.

```
public constructor Channel<T>(capacity: int);
public async method SendAsync(owned item: T, token: CancellationToken := CancellationToken.None): Task;
```

### 7. Sendable cancellation handle
CancellationToken is a borrow-bearing record and cannot cross Domain.Spawn, so graceful shutdown of a domain tree has no interrupt path (a cancel channel cannot abort an in-flight await). Recommend a v1 that is a flag-only sealed sendable class backed by AtomicInteger — pollable plus awaitable (`WaitForCancellationAsync`), with *no* cross-domain Register callbacks in v1 (executing a captured closure on a foreign domain is the unsolved race; awaiting locally sidesteps it). Bridge into the existing model per-domain: a local CancellationTokenSource linked to the handle. Co-design with #810; rationale §12.6 explicitly left this slot open. Hardest design item in the set — needs an RFC, not a direct PR.

### 8. Structured logging (ILogger)
Debug.WriteLine is release-elided and Console.WriteLine has no levels/categories/sinks, so no service can ship. Borrowable interface + LogLevel enum (Trace<Debug<Info<Warning<Error<Critical); concrete ConsoleLogger (Mutex-guarded TextWriter, stdlib §6.2) and NullLogger; cross-domain sink via a logging domain fed by ChannelSender<LogEntry> — both shapes work with today's primitives. Exception data enters as a copied cause-chain snapshot, never a live Exception borrow (§31.1). Structured key-value params wait on variadics; interpolation covers v1.

```
public interface ILogger {
    method IsEnabled(level: LogLevel): bool;
    method Log(level: LogLevel, message: string);
}
```

### 9. Integer toolkit: wrapping/saturating arithmetic + BitOperations + HashCode
Checked-overflow-everywhere (§6.1) with no escape hatch means a 64-bit wrapping multiply — the core of xxHash64, MurmurHash3, FNV-1a — is *unwritable* in Bezel; and every custom IEqualityComparer needs a hash combiner better than XOR. Static methods on the wrapper records (`UInt64.WrappingMul(a, b): ulong`, `Int32.SaturatingAdd`), a `BitOperations` static class (PopCount, LeadingZeroCount, TrailingZeroCount, RotateLeft/Right, IsPow2, Log2), and a `HashCode` accumulator record (`Add<T>(value)` / `ToHashCode(): int`) with a per-process randomized seed (hash-flood defense). All pure value-in/value-out, no ownership or domain questions; directly unblocks #27 (CRC/xxHash).

## Declined-with-reasons

1. **String.Format (runtime positional format)** — interpolation covers compile-time patterns and StringBuilder.AppendFormat covers accumulation; a third entry point adds a second format-string convention (`{0}` vs `{name}`) for a narrow template-from-config use case. Revisit only with evidence.
2. **BigInteger (now)** — no in-tree consumer until System.Security.Cryptography lands; designing it standalone risks a shape crypto can't use. Ride the crypto milestone; record the dependency so crypto is not built on intrinsics.
3. **Metrics API (Counter/Histogram/Gauge, now)** — cross-domain mutable counters are exactly the #1363 static-mutable-state side door; no sound design exists until that ruling lands, and the OTel-shaped surface belongs in an ecosystem package once ILogger + channels exist. Revisit after #1363.
4. **Environment.CurrentDirectory setter** — process-global mutable state visible to all domains fights domain isolation (§22.12 hazard). Ship the getter; child processes take an explicit `workingDirectory` argument (see #5).
5. **Blocking Process.WaitForExit / any sync process wait** — blocks the calling domain in violation of the §30 deadlock discipline; async-only surface.
6. **Compile-time platform branching (cfg/#ifdef)** — a language change, not a stdlib addition; runtime `OperatingSystem.IsLinux()` queries cover the stdlib-scoped need. A conditional-compilation proposal, if ever, goes through the spec workflow.
7. **Overwrite-on-full ring-buffer mode** — silently disposing an element the caller just handed over inverts the ownership contract's legibility; the fault-on-full + TryEnqueue form (P2 backlog) matches the defined-fault philosophy.
8. **Implicit Unicode normalization in string equality** — equality stays ordinal (§9.6 contract); normalization ships only as an explicit transform (`Normalize(form)`, item 31).

## Suggested sequencing

Wave 1 (no deps, high fan-out): #1, #2, #3, #9, #12. Wave 2 (consumes wave 1): #4, #5, #17, #27; plus #6/#8/#11/#13 in parallel. RFC-track concurrently: #7 (sendable cancel) → #15/#16; #10 (tzdata packaging); #24 (`test` modifier spec proposal). Everything ranked ≥18 is additive and can fill lanes opportunistically.
